findings.title: The relief model is 30-80 m too low over the southern Pratzen plateau and the chapel knoll and about 45 m too high at Slapanice, while the visitor is told it is fitted to surveyed elevations
findings.subsystem: relief model (world.js height/localHeight, tools/relief-fit.js, geo.js vertical scale)
findings.user_impact: On the default landscape the ground under the afternoon's central scenes (the I-II Columns' dawn ground, Kamensky, the French guns on the heights over the meres, Napoleon at the chapel) is drawn 120-320 m lower at 4x than survey would give, the plateau's southern half is missing, and the valley fog covers ground that stood above it; nothing tells the visitor.
findings.evidence: Model = GEOREF.elevM(hAt) on the audited sources. Southern box (map x 270-330, y 295-350): model mean 228.1 m vs GLO-90 273.4 m; 32 of 36 cells above the fog top 238.2 m on survey, 9 in the model. Profiles: Pratzeberg-Augezd mean -39 m, worst -82; Sokolnitz-Hostieradek mean -25, worst -82 (model flat about 219 m, survey ridge to 298 m). SRTM 30 m agrees with GLO-90 within 0-7 m at 6 points where the model is 47-81 m low. St Anthony's chapel (OSM point): model 198 m vs 240 m, 8 m above Augezd's 190 m. Slapanice: model 273 m vs 225 m (Wikidata 230). 300 m core grid rms 20.1 m, 18 cells beyond 50 m. Fitted at 12 anchors, none there.
findings.expected: Relief within its method's error over the battle core, or its departures stated where the relief is described (CLAUDE.md: never invent terrain; label uncertainty).
findings.observed: Anchored summits within 0-5 m, departures up to 80 m between anchors; the sources sheet names only reverse stream gradients and the chapel's sight line; the Pratzen place's 'Extent: runs north-south between Blasowitz and the Litava' is not what the relief shows (its high ground ends about 1 km south of the Pratzeberg).
findings.remedy: Before calling the map finished, state the measured departures in the sources sheet and the eye-level note. Then a geographic data task: surveyed anchors on the southern plateau (about 307-311 m at map 288,311; 292-298 m at 297,328), the chapel knoll (about 240 m) and Slapanice (225-230 m) in relief-fit.js, or a DEM-derived grid; re-measure fog extent, knowledge readings, viewsheds, going, self-test pins and motion baselines; CHANGELOG was/is/why.
findings.effort: disclosure 0.5 day; refit 3-8 days with consequences; DEM grid 1-3 weeks
findings.cause_hypothesis: parametric surface (plateau bump 50 x 60 world units, crest ridge 8 units wide, named bumps) fitted at 12 elevation anchors; no southern-plateau or Ricka-valley term
findings.cause_verified: yes: relief-fit.js anchors and TERMS read
findings.validation: re-run dem.js --analyse, plateau.js, extra.js: southern box mean within 10 m, profiles' worst within 20 m, Slapanice within 10 m
findings.risk: moves fog, knowledge, viewsheds, going, cover thresholds and dependent baselines

findings.title: Between Girzikowitz and Sokolnitz the drawn Goldbach departs up to about 300 m from today's channel and puts Girzikowitz and Kobelnitz on the opposite bank
findings.user_impact: The armies' dividing line runs east of Girzikowitz and Kobelnitz on the map and west of both today: the kind of bank error 8J corrected at Sokolnitz.
findings.evidence: Today's Goldbach = OSM Roketnice to its mouth at map (202.6,225.3), then the Ricka. Girzikowitz: drawn bed 172 m east of the village, today's 170 m west; Kobelnitz: drawn 79 m east, today's 91 m west; Puntowitz and Sokolnitz same bank in both. sthilaire@2 'Crosses the Goldbach and forms for the attack' is 146 m west of the drawn bed and 62 m east of today's. Reach y 212-300 50-340 m off today's channel.
findings.expected: The bed where period evidence puts it, or marked unverified.
findings.observed: Four straight legacy vertices; no period map read north of y 309.8 (world.js:47), though 8H obtained the 1825 Kobelnitz sketch.
findings.remedy: Georeference the 1825 sketches of Kobylnice (held) and Jirikovice, then a geographic data task on GOLDBACH_M with the anchors' sides recomputed; until then say the course there is unverified.
findings.judgement_kind: measured against modern channels; 1805 not established

findings.title: Outside Sokolnitz the hydrography is schematic and unlabelled: the Bosenitz brook and the Ricka through Slapanice are not drawn, and the upper Goldbach runs where no stream runs today
findings.user_impact: No stream at the Santon's foot or through Slapanice, a Goldbach source 1.1 km east of the Santon, brooks up to 1.8 km from any watercourse, with no sign of uncertainty (only the meres say 'schematic'); four French cavalry divisions are drawn crossing a reach that does not exist today.
findings.evidence: Tvarozensky potok: 4.65 km in the frame, 51 m from Bosenitz and 131 m from the Santon, all over 300 m (up to 3.0 km) from any drawn stream; the Ricka from the NW edge through Slapanice: 12.2 km over 300 m (up to 6.4 km); drawn Goldbach y 109-176: 275-1,153 m from any modern stream; BROOKS[2] median 772 m (max 1,828) and BROOKS[0] 208 m from OSM's nearest waterway. Kellermann, Nansouty, d'Hautpoul, Walther 0->5 cross the drawn upper Goldbach at y 127-152.
findings.expected: Streams from evidence or labelled schematic, as the meres are (decision 27).
findings.observed: Only a code comment calls the Rakovec schematic (world.js:59); no legend row for streams; the Goldbach place states its course (unchecked).
findings.remedy: Quick: a legend row and a sources-sheet sentence on the streams' schematic courses. Then a geographic data task drawing the Bosenitz brook and the Ricka from the 1825-52 maps and checking the upper Goldbach and BROOKS[2]; re-measure crossings and the relief carve.

findings.title: Sokolnitz, Telnitz and Kobelnitz are drawn standing in marsh: marsh ellipses cover their centres and the cover classifier ranks marsh above village
findings.user_impact: The three villages fought over all morning stand on marsh ground on the landscape; 81-92% of their buildings sit on the marsh or water class.
findings.evidence: Planner records in node: on the village class Sokolnitz 4/27, Telnitz 2/25, Kobelnitz 3/16 (Puntowitz 14/19, Satschan 10/14; all 309/377). Centres inside MARSH[0] (Sokolnitz 0.57, Telnitz 0.57), MARSH[1-2] (Telnitz), MARSH[4] and [6] (Kobelnitz 0.25, 0.28). coverClass returns water and marsh before village. 8H's page measure 0%, 5%, 19%, 74%; open since 8G.
findings.expected: Villages on dry ground in their own class, the marsh beside them.
findings.observed: As evidence; recorded open, no owner decision.
findings.remedy: Geographic data task: village before marsh inside a village's place, or MARSH kept off the villages; re-measure cover fractions, going and the self-test's cover and buildings checks.

findings.title: The Goldbach bottom's marshiness, an open question, is drawn and told as settled, and no check can fail a stream or marsh crossing
findings.subsystem: land cover and narrative (MARSH, TERRAIN_LINES, FEATURES goldbach, TOUR[0]); movement audit
findings.user_impact: The opening's first step tells a first-time visitor the Goldbach runs 'in a marshy bottom' and the map draws marsh ellipses 1-2 km across round Telnitz, while the project lists December 1805's marshiness as unresolved (the meres were frozen that day).
findings.evidence: TOUR[0].x and FEATURES[#goldbach].sub/facts have no claim; the terrain line's note is outside the inventory; MARSH[0]'s comment: rests on that note, not re-examined. 46 legs touch drawn marsh or water; kienmayer 2->7 lies wholly on marsh (664 m); 9 anchors on marsh, 20 on water; 30 of 50 stream crossings away from any village place or road crossing. crossingProblem tests ponds and marsh only and exempts points within 22 map units (695 m) of any village: 0 findings.
findings.expected: The open question shown where the claim is made (as the vineyard's legend row does) and a rule that can fail a crossing.
findings.observed: Settled wording on the primary path; the question absent from SOURCE_NOTE's list; streams never tested.
findings.remedy: Reword or label the marsh statements, add the question to the open questions and a qualifier to marsh; add stream crossings away from villages and roads to the movement audit.
prior_refs: history: interpolated legs across the Litava; the movement audit tests neither

findings.title: 'Walled castle' and 'pheasantry enclosure' are stated as fact in the 08:00 dispatch, against the project's own records
findings.subsystem: narrative and landmarks (PHASES[2].lede, FEATURES[#sokolnitz].sub, prz@2 act)
findings.user_impact: The Now tab's 08:00 dispatch, untagged, says the columns attack 'its walled castle and the pheasantry enclosure'; the castle is drawn without a wall, the 1825 sketch draws none round the pheasantry, and the castle's walls are on the unresolved list.
findings.evidence: PHASES[#2].lede, FEATURES[#sokolnitz].sub and prz@2's act carry no claim; paintDispatch writes the lede untagged; narrative.js:91: 'The castle's walls and the pheasantry's enclosure are this map's record, not checked here.'; appearance.js: the orchard wall disputed, not drawn; 8H G2: no wall drawn in 1825.
findings.expected: An unresolved question not stated as settled on the primary path.
findings.observed: Settled in the dispatch; unchecked tags only in dossiers.
findings.remedy: Data task (text): drop or attribute 'walled' and 'enclosure', claims added, chronology L9 rehash if touched.

findings.title: Krug is drawn 1.67 km south of where the 1836-52 survey and today's map put it, and the visitor is told no source read fixes it
findings.user_impact: Bagration's outposts 'in Krug and Holubitz' read as a line 1.6 km long north to south; the two places adjoin (Kruh 0.56 km WNW of Holubitz).
findings.evidence: Drawn Krug [339,139] 1,671 m at 359 deg from Wikidata's Kruh, which lies 562 m at 288 deg from drawn Holubitz; Bellowitz 1,302 m from Bedrichovice. SOURCE_NOTE: 'which no source read fixes'. 8K's register read the Second Survey's 'Kruch' immediately west of Holubitz (the grade on which 8K moved the post and road) and gives the drawn Krug as '2.9 km away' (measured 1.67 km).
findings.expected: A place drawn on the evidence read, or its distance stated; the register's figure correct.
findings.remedy: Candidate data task: Krug to the Second Survey's Kruch (C for 1805), Bellowitz to its RUIAN point as Turas was, bag@0's act checked; until then correct the note and the register's 2.9 km.
prior_refs: history: open questions drawn or shown without qualification: Krug and Bellowitz

findings.title: The Pratzen church is drawn 161 m from its read site while the sources sheet says it is drawn at its own site

findings.evidence: Planner record at map (281.33,252.89), 161 m from LANDMARK_SITES.church.Pratzen (277.0,255.6). The legacy straight Pratzen-Sokolnitz track ('course unverified') passes 72 m from the site and its ribbon's clearance moves the church. The self-test admits 5 world units (316 m). Node, same code and default factor as the page's boot plan.
findings.expected: Drawn at its site, or the sheet stating the offset; a tolerance near the church's size.
findings.remedy: State the offset, or let a read landmark site displace the unverified track; tighten the self-test's tolerance for read sites.

8J and 8K's corrections reproduce independently: the Sokolnitz bed within 1-6 m of today's channel, the highway within 3 m median of OSM's road 430, the castle and Pratzen church sites within 4-7 m, the garden within 3 m, the post house within 2-16 m.
